div.head: ECf 32 A 9
div.ab: Debent etiam uniuersi liberi homines totius regni, iuxta facultates suas et possessiones suas et secundum catalla sua et iuxta feodum suum et secundum tenementa sua, arma habere et illa semper prompta conseruare ad tuitionem regni et ad seruitium dominorum suorum iuxta preceptum domini regis explendum et peragendum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 656 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

Liebermann prints some words here in smaller type (liberi homines, catalla, feodum, arma habere, seruitium dominorum, preceptum domini regis); they are taken over from the Assize of Arms of 1181, which his margin names.

note.seg: ähnlich Wl art. retr. 8; auch Ine schon schob der Londoner Verbot der Waffenausfuhr unter; mein Leges Angl. S. 12
similarly Wl art. retr. 8; the Londoner already slipped a ban on the export of arms into Ine too; my Leges Angl. p. 12

seg.hi: diese Rücksicht auf die adligen Lehnsherren führt der Londoner ein

note.seg: the Londoner introduces this regard for the noble feudal lords

div.ab: All the free men of the whole kingdom also must, according to their means and their possessions, and according to their chattels, and according to their fee, and according to their tenements, have arms and always keep them ready for the defence of the kingdom and for fulfilling and performing the service of their lords according to the command of the lord king.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Heer 2d. 12; Waffe 10a. Verf. macht die Wehrpflicht zumeist dem Lehnwesen (s. d. Gl 10; u. 15) dienstbar; staatsbürgerliche Landwehr tuitio regni findet schwächeren Ausdruck. — 2catella Rs
Cf. Gl Heer 2d. 12; Waffe 10a. The author makes military duty serve mostly feudalism (see that word in Gl 10; below, 15); the citizens' militia, tuitio regni, finds weaker expression. — 2catella Rs
